transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I'm here today because I've been feeling extremely down and have completely lost interest in everything for the past five months. I have absolutely no motivation to do anything, even the things I used to enjoy. It has just been really hard to keep going like this.
Have you felt depressed or lost interest most days for at least two years, or did this episode start only within the last few months?
No, it definitely hasn't been going on for two years. These feelings of depression and loss of interest started just recently, about five months ago. Before that, things were quite different.
Have you also had changes in sleep or appetite during these five months?

Yes, my appetite has dropped significantly, and I've actually lost a noticeable amount of weight because I barely feel like eating. However, I haven't really noticed any specific changes in my sleep patterns during this time.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or feeling like life isn't worth living. Even though things have been really tough and I feel very down, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.
Have you noticed feeling slowed down or agitated, or has it been hard to concentrate on things during this time?

I don't really feel slowed down or have trouble concentrating, but during my high periods, I get extremely agitated and restless. I can't tolerate resting or sitting still at all, and I always feel driven by this overwhelming, restless energy to keep moving and doing things.
During those high periods, have you ever had a time lasting at least one week where you felt unusually energized or irritable with less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or risky behavior?

Yes, I've had those high periods, and they actually lasted for about two months. I felt overflowing with energy, but I would also get extremely irritated and angry over the smallest things. During those times, I ended up doing some really impulsive and risky things without thinking about the consequences.
Did those high periods ever cause major problems like needing hospitalization, losing touch with reality, or being unable to function at work or home?

No, I never needed to be hospitalized or lost touch with reality during those times. However, I did cause some major problems by going on reckless buying sprees and spending huge amounts of money we didn't have. It ended up causing a lot of financial distress for myself and my family.
During those high periods, were you still able to function at work, school, and home, or did the symptoms make it impossible to keep up with your usual responsibilities?

During those high periods, I actually felt the opposite of unable to function—I was hyperactive, starting multiple projects and doing far more work than usual. However, that high energy also led to impulsive decisions like reckless spending and making rash business investments. So it didn't stop me from keeping up with responsibilities, but I made some very foolish choices.
Have you ever had a period like that that was so severe it caused marked impairment, psychosis, or required hospitalization?
No, I don't think it has ever been that severe. I've never been hospitalized, and I have never experienced anything like psychosis.
Based on your answers, the pattern is most consistent with Bipolar II Disorder rather than Bipolar I Disorder. Would you like me to explain why?
Yes, please, I would really like to hear your explanation. How do my symptoms of elevated, irritable moods and these periods of low energy and loss of interest distinguish Bipolar II from Bipolar I?
